claims.text: Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by competition between thermodynamic and kinetic factors.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be predicted using DFT-calculated pairwise interactions among its constituent elements.
The initial state of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is high-temperature BCC.
The proposed intervention is controlled cooling from 1000°C to 500°C at 5°C/min.
Cooling is to be performed under vacuum with no external stress.
Pairwise interactions among Cr, Co, Fe, Ni, and Al atoms are the mediator of phase stability.
Composition-dependent pairwise interactions drive thermodynamic instability.
The proposed thermodynamic instability promotes formation of secondary phases.
Controlled cooling will produce a 20% increase in secondary-phase fraction relative to the as-cast baseline.
The secondary phases formed may include sigma and mu phases.
Secondary-phase fraction can be assessed by X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy.
The baseline is as-cast Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 in a high-temperature BCC state.
The proposed hypothesis applies from 500°C to 1000°C and at cooling rates from 1°C/min to 10°C/min.
A secondary-phase increase of less than 10%, or a decrease, relative to baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says phase stability is governed by competition between thermodynamic and kinetic factors, but the stated mechanism specifies only thermodynamic instability and does not identify a kinetic mediator or explain how cooling rate enters the competition.
